lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay, so where do we want to start with this fridge app idea?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I think we start with the core loop. You photograph what's in your fridge, and we suggest three things you could actually cook tonight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three feels right. More than that and people freeze up.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. And the suggestions have to respect what you don't have, not just what you do.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the whole trick, honestly. I've had it happen to me a dozen times, a recipe that needs two things I didn't buy.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So, point one. Suggestions are limited to what's on hand, plus a short pantry list we assume everyone has.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Salt, oil, flour, that kind of thing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Second thing I keep coming back to is speed. If it takes longer than about ten seconds from photo to suggestions, I'd just order takeout.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Agreed. Ten seconds is the bar.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Third, I want it to learn a little. If you skip the same recipe four times, stop showing it to me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mm, that's a nice one. Low effort, feels smart.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fourth, a shopping nudge. Not a full grocery list, just, you're one ingredient away from three more meals.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, I like that a lot. That's the bit someone would screenshot.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fifth, and this one's less fun. We need some way to handle leftovers. Half a lemon, a bit of rice.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yeah. Leftovers are most of the real problem.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Alright, let's decide something concrete. For the first build, we do photo in, three suggestions out, and nothing else.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Let's commit to that. No accounts, no social feed, no meal planning calendar for version one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Decided then. Photo to three suggestions, and we cut everything else.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: One thing I genuinely don't know is how good the recognition has to be before it stops feeling like a toy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the open question, isn't it. Does it need to see every single item, or is roughly right fine as long as the suggestions are good?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I don't have an answer. We should try it on a few real fridges before we tune anything.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Let's leave it open and come back to it after the first prototype.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Works for me.
